evidence: Tac. Agr. 42.2: salārium tamen prōcōnsulāre solitum offerrī
Suet. Tib. 46: numquam salāriō, cibāriīs tantum sustentāvit
Plin. Ep. 4.12.2: ante lēgitimum salāriī tempus
M-O s.v. salary, pay (of employees), wages
terms.comment: In imperial prose the fixed pay of officials and of the emperor’s companions (Lewis & Short); the source of the English word. Pliny says it was named from salt (NH 31.89, Lewis & Short).

evidence: Traupman 373: aequam mercēdem alicui solvere, to pay someone a fair salary
M-O s.v. salary, pay (of employees), wages
terms.comment: Pay for work of any kind (see wage); Traupman’s word for a salary.

evidence: Liv. 1.20.3: stīpendium dē pūblicō statuit, (Numa) gave (the Vestals) a salary from public funds
M-O s.v. salary, pay (of employees), wages
terms.comment: The soldier’s pay (Caes., Liv.), and so any regular stipend (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Pecūniae parcus ac tenāx comitēs peregrīnātiōnum expedītiōnumque numquam salāriō, cibāriīs tantum sustentāvit
phrases.english: Sparing and close with money, he never kept the companions of his travels and campaigns on a salary, only on their food

phrases.latin: Salārium tamen prōcōnsulāre solitum offerrī et quibusdam ā sē ipsō concessum Agricolae nōn dedit
phrases.english: But the salary of a proconsul, which was usually offered, and which he had himself granted to some, he did not give Agricola
to pay someone a fair salary
